# PillaiBrauer — runs where no member is coprime to all the others

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proof drafted, not yet built

Among any 16 or fewer consecutive positive integers one is coprime to all the others (Pillai, cited). From 17 on this fails, through the wheels up to 13. The run 2184 to 2200 has every member sharing one of the wheels 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 with another member, and shifting it by any multiple of their combined cycle 30030 keeps that, so there are infinitely many such runs.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [M. Waldschmidt, S. S. Pillai's work on consecutive integers (lecture notes, 2006)](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/%7Emichel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/Kumbakonam21122006.pdf) — states both halves and the run from 2184 with shifts by multiples of 30030
- [Arithmetic Progressions in a Unique Factorization Domain (arXiv:1108.1267)](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1108.1267) — history of Pillai's and Brauer's results and the arithmetic-progression form

## Claims

<a id="pillai_sixteen"></a>
### `pillai_sixteen`

Any run of 1 to 16 consecutive positive integers has a member coprime to every other member (cited).

```lean
/-- **Pillai's theorem** (cited). Any run of between 1 and 16 consecutive
positive integers contains a member coprime to every other member. -/
def pillai_sixteen : Prop :=
  ∀ n k : Nat, 1 ≤ n → 1 ≤ k → k ≤ 16 →
    ∃ i < k, ∀ j < k, j ≠ i → Nat.Coprime (n + i) (n + j)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Justification:** cited — S. S. Pillai (1940), as stated in M. Waldschmidt's notes on Pillai's work (exact paper reference to be checked), main theorem. Not proved in Lean.

<a id="pillai_witness_17"></a>
### `pillai_witness_17`

Each of 2184, ..., 2200 shares one of the wheels 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 with another member of the run.

```lean
/-- **The run of 17 from 2184.** Each of 2184, ..., 2200 shares one of the
wheels 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 with some other member of the run. -/
def pillai_witness_17 : Prop :=
  ∀ i < 17, ∃ j < 17, j ≠ i ∧ ∃ p ∈ small_wheels, p ∣ 2184 + i ∧ p ∣ 2184 + j
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.PillaiBrauer.pillai_witness_17_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/PillaiBrauer.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PillaiBrauer.lean)

<a id="pillai_witness_17_repeats"></a>
### `pillai_witness_17_repeats`

Shifting the run from 2184 by any multiple of the cycle 30030 gives a run of 17 where no member is coprime to all the others.

```lean
/-- **The run repeats with the cycle.** For every number of cycles `m`, in the
run of 17 starting at `30030 * m + 2184` no member is coprime to all the
others. -/
def pillai_witness_17_repeats : Prop :=
  ∀ m : Nat, ∀ i < 17, ∃ j < 17, j ≠ i ∧
    1 < Nat.gcd (30030 * m + 2184 + i) (30030 * m + 2184 + j)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.PillaiBrauer.pillai_witness_17_repeats_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/PillaiBrauer.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PillaiBrauer.lean)
